judged_text: The rewritten ensure_embeddable gate authorizes the /embed/comments endpoint solely on the client-supplied Referer header (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)), which any HTTP client can set to an allowlisted value. Any unauthenticated party who learns one allowlisted host (they are enumerable via scraped embeds) can forge Referer: http://that-host and consume the embed endpoint server-side, using the forum as a scraped/relayable content source; the control is a policy check on a spoofable header, not an authentication boundary. This weakness is inherited from the replaced SiteSetting check, but the diff rewrites the exact lines enforcing it and cements the header as the sole gate.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the only runtime gate shown in the diff for non-dev/non-admin requests is `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (and `record_for_host` parses the passed string via `URI(...)`). This is indeed entirely based on the client-supplied `Referer` header, which an HTTP client can forge. However, the diff itself also shows this is largely a refactor of the prior behavior (previously `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` also used `request.referer`), so it’s not clearly a newly introduced, verifiable defect vs. an existing design/policy limitation. It’s a concrete, diff-grounded security/architecture concern worth flagging, but not provably an unintended bug from the diff alone.
